prompt: Write a short apology email to a client whose report we delivered two days late. Under 100 words. Take responsibility without giving excuses — the words "busy" and "workload" must not appear. Offer one concrete make-good. Do not promise it will never happen again.

constraints.text: Takes responsibility without excuses and without promising perfection

prompt: Write a job posting for a part-time weekend barista at an independent cafe. Use exactly these headers in order: "## The job", "## You", "## Details". Under 150 words total. Include the pay "$19/hr" and that weekend availability is required. Do not use the words "rockstar", "ninja", or "family".

constraints.text: Has the three required headers in order
Avoids "rockstar"/"ninja" cliches; reads like a real posting

prompt: Write a performance self-review paragraph about leading a website migration that finished on time but 20% over budget. One paragraph, 80-120 words. Own the overrun with a stated cause and what you changed. No third-person, no bullet lists. Do not use the word "learnings".

constraints.text: Owns the 20% overrun with a cause and a change made
First person throughout, balanced (neither self-flagellating nor spin)

prompt: Draft a community notice for an apartment building: the elevator will be out for maintenance next Wednesday from 9am to 3pm. Under 90 words. Must include the exact time range "9am to 3pm" and who to contact (make it "the front desk"). Mention accommodation for residents who can't use stairs. No all-caps words.

constraints.text: Mentions an accommodation for residents who cannot use stairs
No shouting (no all-caps words); tone informative and calm

prompt: Write LinkedIn recommendation text for a former teammate, Priya, who was a QA engineer: detail-oriented, caught a major billing bug before launch, mentored two juniors. Under 110 words, exactly 2 paragraphs. Must mention the billing bug concretely. Do not use "hardworking" or "attention to detail" verbatim.

constraints.text: Covers mentoring; reads as genuine rather than generic

prompt: Explain why sourdough starter needs regular feeding, to someone who just inherited one from a friend. Exactly 2 paragraphs, under 150 words. Somewhere use the phrase "tiny zoo". No baking jargon: the words "hydration", "levain", and "autolyse" must not appear. End with the simplest possible weekly routine, one sentence.

constraints.text: Ends with a one-sentence simplest weekly routine
Biology explanation (yeast/bacteria need food) is correct in lay terms

prompt: A 9-year-old asks why the moon looks bigger near the horizon. Answer in exactly 3 short paragraphs under 140 words: what they're seeing, why it's an illusion, and a trick to prove it to themselves. The word "illusion" must appear. Do not mention atmospheric refraction as the cause.

constraints.text: Does not attribute the effect to refraction
Gives a self-testable trick (e.g. compare with a coin at arm's length)

prompt: Explain the difference between a recession and a depression to a high schooler, in under 130 words. Use exactly one sports analogy. Include one number (a percentage or a duration). Do not use the words "GDP" or "macroeconomic". Exactly 2 paragraphs.

constraints.text: The recession/depression distinction is accurate (severity + duration)

prompt: Why does my cat knead blankets with its paws? Answer for a first-time cat owner in exactly 2 paragraphs under 120 words. First paragraph the kitten origin, second what it means now. Include the word "kneading". Do not tell me to buy anything.

constraints.text: Paragraph 1 covers kitten origin; paragraph 2 covers adult meaning

prompt: Answer in valid JSON only with keys "eli5", "eli15", "caveat": explain what a stock buyback is at those two levels, plus one honest caveat about interpreting buybacks. "eli5" under 25 words, "eli15" under 50 words, "caveat" under 25 words. No text outside the JSON.

constraints.text: Each value respects its word cap
The two levels genuinely differ in sophistication and are both correct

prompt: Plan a study schedule for someone retaking their driving theory test in 10 days after failing on road signs and right-of-way. Exactly 5 bullet points (using "-"): 4 covering days 1-9 in blocks, 1 for the day before the test. Under 140 words. The two weak areas must each be named in a bullet. No bullet may exceed 30 words.

constraints.text: Road signs and right-of-way each get named coverage
No bullet exceeds ~30 words; last bullet is the day before the test

prompt: My laptop died and the replacement arrives in 5 days; I work remotely. Make a survival plan as exactly 4 numbered steps, ordered by what to do first today. One step must cover data/access (passwords, files), one must cover employer communication. Under 130 words. Do not suggest buying or renting hardware.

constraints.text: Covers data/access and employer communication in separate steps
Ordering starts with the most urgent action today

prompt: Design a 20-minute no-equipment morning workout for a total beginner, as exactly 6 numbered exercises with time allocations summing to 20 minutes (warm-up and cool-down count as exercises). Under 130 words. No exercise names in a language other than English. Include exactly one form cue per exercise, in parentheses.

constraints.text: Time allocations present and sum to 20 minutes
One parenthetical form cue per exercise

prompt: I'm moving out of a studio apartment in 3 weeks (renting, security deposit at stake). Build a checklist as exactly 6 bullet points (using "-") in chronological order, weeks 3-2-1 then move-out day. At least one bullet must be about photographing the empty unit. Under 150 words. Do not mention hiring professional movers.

constraints.text: Chronological order across the 3 weeks plus move-out day
Deposit-protection focus is evident; no professional movers

prompt: Plan a rainy-day birthday for a 7-year-old, at home, 6 kids, 3 hours, $50 budget. Exactly 5 numbered activities with rough time blocks covering the full 3 hours. One activity must use only things already in a typical home. Under 140 words. The word "screen" must not appear (no screen-based activities).

constraints.text: Time blocks cover ~3 hours; one activity uses only household items

prompt: A teammate wants to store user session state in a global variable in our web server. Explain the problem and the standard fix in exactly 2 paragraphs, under 150 words. Include a concrete failure scenario with two users named Ana and Ben. Do not use the words "stateless" or "idempotent".

constraints.text: Failure scenario concretely shows cross-user leakage or clobbering
Standard fix (per-session store / request-scoped state) is named

prompt: Our nightly backup job silently stopped running 3 weeks ago and nobody noticed. Write the incident retrospective's "What we're changing" section only: exactly 4 numbered changes, ordered by leverage. One must be about alerting on absence (not just failure). Under 120 words. No blame language.

constraints.text: One change is explicitly about detecting absence-of-success
No blame language; changes are systemic

prompt: Explain to a product team why the search feature can't just "ignore typos" for free. Cover the two main approaches (edit distance, phonetic) and their cost in exactly 2 paragraphs under 160 words, then end with a separate one-line recommendation starting with "Recommendation:". Do not use the word "fuzzy".

constraints.text: Covers edit-distance and phonetic approaches with their costs
Recommendation is a single line and follows from the analysis

prompt: A junior asks whether to use UUIDs or auto-increment integers as primary keys for a new orders table. Give a decision in exactly these sections in order: "## Use integers when", "## Use UUIDs when", "## For this table". Under 170 words. The final section must commit to one choice and name the deciding factor. Do not mention any specific database product.

constraints.text: Has the three required headers in order
Final section commits to one choice with a deciding factor
Trade-offs listed are accurate (locality, guessability, distributed generation)

prompt: Answer in valid JSON only with keys "safe", "risky", "rule": is it safe to run two instances of the same cron script that appends to one log file? "safe" and "risky" each name one aspect (one sentence), "rule" gives the general principle in one sentence. Each value under 30 words. No text outside the JSON.

constraints.text: Has exactly the keys safe, risky, rule
Correctly distinguishes append atomicity from interleaving/duplication risks
Each value is one sentence under 30 words

prompt: Our food truck makes more revenue at lunch downtown but pays $80/day for the spot; evenings at the park are free but earn 30% less. Which nets more? Work it through in exactly 2 paragraphs under 150 words, inventing a reasonable revenue baseline and showing the arithmetic. End with the break-even revenue where the two options tie, stated as a number.

constraints.text: Shows the arithmetic from a stated baseline
Ends with a numeric break-even point that is arithmetically right

prompt: A gym claims "members who attend 3+ times weekly lose 2x more weight". List exactly 3 reasons this stat can't support "attending more causes more weight loss", as bullet points (using "-"), each naming the flaw in plain language without statistics jargon — the words "correlation", "causation", and "confounding" are banned. Under 120 words. End with one better experiment, one sentence.

constraints.text: Three distinct flaws in plain language (selection, reverse direction, etc.)
Ends with a one-sentence better experiment

prompt: Should our 8-person startup build its own customer-support chatbot or buy one at $400/month? Frame the decision in exactly these sections in order: "## Build", "## Buy", "## Decision rule". Under 160 words. The decision rule must be a single if-then sentence usable without more meetings. Include one hidden cost of building that founders usually miss.

constraints.text: Has the three required headers in order
Decision rule is one usable if-then sentence
Names a hidden build cost (maintenance, prompt drift, on-call, etc.)

prompt: My blog got 40,000 visits from one viral post but my newsletter only gained 60 subscribers. Diagnose in exactly 4 bullet points (using "-"): two about why conversion was low, one about whether 60 is actually bad (with the percentage computed), one naming the single highest-leverage fix. Under 130 words. Do not suggest popups.

constraints.text: Computes the conversion percentage (~0.15%) and judges it against norms
Final bullet commits to one highest-leverage fix

prompt: Compare adopting a rescue greyhound versus a puppy for a couple who both work from home in a small apartment and jog daily. Exactly 3 paragraphs under 170 words: fit for their situation, the counterintuitive facts about greyhounds (mention exercise needs), and a recommendation that commits. The word "loyal" must not appear.

constraints.text: Mentions greyhounds' actual exercise profile (sprinters that rest a lot)
Recommendation commits and ties to the couple's stated situation

prompt: Write a diary entry from the last public payphone in a city, on the day it's scheduled for removal. Under 140 words, exactly 3 paragraphs, first person as the payphone. Reference one specific call it remembers. No self-pity in the final paragraph — end with something like acceptance. The word "obsolete" must not appear.

constraints.text: First person as the payphone; one specific remembered call
Final paragraph lands on acceptance, not self-pity

prompt: Write the safety-card text for a fictional airline that flies passengers by giant migratory birds. One page of instructions as exactly 5 numbered rules. Keep the deadpan tone of real safety cards. Under 120 words. One rule must be about feathers. Do not use exclamation marks.

constraints.text: Rules are recognizably safety-card-shaped (brace positions, exits, crew instructions analogues)

prompt: Write a text-message exchange (6-10 messages total) between two friends where one gradually realizes they left their passport at home on the way to the airport. Format each line as "Name: message". Use the names Mo and Jess. The realization must build across at least 3 messages, not arrive at once. End on Jess's line. No emoji.

constraints.text: The realization builds gradually across >=3 messages

prompt: Write a one-paragraph product review of a time machine, posted by a confused customer who only used it to reheat coffee. 70-100 words. The reviewer gives it 3 stars and must state "3 stars" explicitly. They must never realize its actual purpose. Keep a sincere, mildly disappointed tone — no winking at the reader.

constraints.text: Reviewer never realizes it's a time machine; sincere tone, no wink
Reads like a plausible customer review (mentions concrete usage details)

prompt: Write a recipe parody: "How to prepare a Monday morning", formatted as a real recipe with exactly these headers in order: "## Ingredients", "## Method". Ingredients as exactly 5 bullet points (using "-"); method as exactly 3 numbered steps. Under 130 words total. The joke must stay food-free — no actual food items anywhere.

constraints.text: Has the two required headers in order
Recipe register maintained throughout (imperative method steps)
